# gridtracker2

**Live map of FT8/JS8 activity, fed by WSJT-X and JS8Call**

- **Version recorded:** 2.260812.0
- **Categories:** `weak-signal`
- **Upstream:** <https://gridtracker.org/>

## What it does

Listens to WSJT-X or JS8Call over UDP and draws every decode on a live world map by grid square -- who is being heard where, on which band, in real time. Tracks wanted grids, states and DXCC entities against your log, and can send spots onward to PSK Reporter.

## Why you would want it

FT8 without a map is a list of callsigns; with GridTracker it becomes situational awareness -- band openings are visible as they happen, and a needed grid lights up the moment it transmits. The de facto companion to WSJT-X. GridTracker2 is the maintained successor to the original GridTracker that AHRL v26 shipped.

## Before it will work

WSJT-X or JS8Call running with UDP reporting enabled (WSJT-X: Settings -> Reporting -> UDP Server). No radio access of its own -- everything arrives over the network from the decoder.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install gridtracker2 --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## Known problems

An Electron application, so the .deb is large (~110 MB) and CPU/RAM use is browser-class -- relevant on a Raspberry Pi. The vendor .deb installs to /opt and provides its own desktop entry.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Releases land in the GitLab package registry (gitlab.com/gridtracker.org/gridtracker2), versioned by date like 2.260812.0. No probe method reads a GitLab registry yet; when one exists this manifest is its first user.
